tei:titleStmt.tei:title: יוֹם הַבִּכּוּרִים
Yom ha-Bikkurim, the bikkur piyyuṭ for the first day of Shavˁuot in the Old French and Romaniote Rites

tei:div.tei:head: Yom ha-Bikkurim, the bikkur piyyuṭ for the first day of Shavˁuot in the Old French and Romaniote Rites

tei:lg.tei:l: The first-fruits day, you will offer a new grain-offering
Two, two-tenths, scalded and in a pancake.
In clamorous tumultuous Salem, the foundation stone,
Exultant, it is sanctified in ten degrees of holiness.
At the end of the fifty, in the third, on the sixth,
Moshe commanded us a Teaching, an inheritance. (Deuteronomy 33:4)
And two sheep for peace-offerings, one year old,
Loaded northerly and eaten in sanctity by the male priests,
And two loaves sanctified like an offering, baked leavened,
Permitting new-grain in the Temple like the ˁomer in the land,
My Sovereign will set them as of old to the faithful city.
And the Cause’s redeemed will return, and Ẓion will come in joy. (Isaiah 51:11)
Semolina bakes on festivals, but does not override the delight.
From the prior weekday’s eve they set up the grain-offering.
And seven sheep, and an ox, and rams whole-burnt altarwards,
And a goat of atonement beside the day’s additions and individual offerings.
”For sin” is not mentioned that the Sovereign’s word be restful.
Joy and happiness will take them, while sorrow and groaning flee. (Isaiah 35:10)
Your blossoming priests, o Ẓion, your pious singers,
they endiademed your beauty in your splendid garb.
Harvesters and celebrants repaid sevenfold your season’s remnants.
On a Sunday sacrifice-day, the priest wears no precious garb,
In the power of your cherishing and sweetness of your love,
They will say to Jerusalem, “Be dwelt, Ẓion, hands undrooped!!” (Zephaniah 3:16)
Children of Jeshurun, they are your builders.
The peoples will call to the Mountain at your timed occurences.
And your oppressor’s’ children will come bowing before you. (Isaiah 60:14)
Your counters will be drunk on their wine-like blood.
Princesses your nursemaids, and kings your nannies.
And all your children will be the Cause’s students, and great your children’s peace. (Isaiah 54:13)

tei:note.tei:p: two traits that are forbidden for the leḥem ˁoni of Pesaḥ, according to Bavli Pesaḥim 36b. The payṭan is here using them to distinguish the relatively luxurious bread offered on Shavuˁot.
referring to Jerusalem. For “clamorous, tumultuous, exultant” find Isaiah 22:2
at the end of the fifty-day ˁomer-counting period, on the third month of Sivan, on the sixth day on the month
find Mishnah Zevaḥim 5:5, for instructions for the communal peace-offerings.
other than the thanksgiving offering, the first-fruits offering on Shavuˁot is the only time leavened bread is used in the Temple.
in Numbers 28:30, the sacrifice for Shavuˁot. All other places in the chapter where an atonement-goat is required, the word “for sin” is included. Find Yerushalmi Rosh haShanah 4:8.
from here until the end of the poem, the payṭan speaks to Ẓion in the second person.

Shavuˁot is a one-day holiday but for the six days after it the sacrifice is also accepted. Find Bavli Ḥagigah 17a. This is also why many communities don’t recite taḥanun for the week after Shavuˁot — find Mishnah Brurah 131:36.

find Mishnah Ḥagigah 2:4. When Shavuˁot fell on a Shabbat, the day the animals would be sacrificed would fall on the Sunday afterwards, but the high priest would wear his regular clothing instead of his festive garments.
a metaphorical statement of vengeance on oppressors, but sounding close enough to blood libel accusations that this line was redacted from several manuscripts by the censors.
